messages:
ana: Quick sync — we need to lock the embeddings endpoint behavior for the next sprint. Key asks from customers: support up to 4096 dims, predictable per-item shapes for downstream FAISS indexes, and a path for older clients that only expect 512/1024 dims. Can we decide shape handling + batching constraints today?

matt: short answer: we can support multiple dims, but mixing different dim vectors in the same response is painful for most clients. we should define one of: single-dim-per-request OR provide per-item dim metadata.

sasha: +1. proposal: require a single canonical dimension per request (server validates). if clients want mixed dims they must call multiple requests or use a multi-response streaming form. simplifies memory layout and batching.

product_beth: customers insist on single-shape outputs: it simplifies storing vectors and building indexes. but they also want an upgrade path. Could we offer a compatibility mode: "pad_to_dim" or "truncate_to_dim"?

jamal: pad/truncate mode is doable. tradeoffs: padding wastes memory and I/O; truncation loses signal. we should cap padded zeros to avoid surprising huge payloads. also need a per-request limit on total elements to keep GPU memory predictable.

ana (typo fix): sorry, that was me — ana.

matt: suggested limits: max_items_per_request = 256, max_total_dimensions = 1_048_576 (items * dim <= 1_048_576). this keeps worst-case memory bounded. e.g., 256 * 4096 = 1,048,576. default to max_items 64 for public tier.

sasha: sounds good. we should also enforce a max_payload_bytes ceiling. also: if user asks for 4096 but model available only at 2048, we should return a clear 409 response that suggests alternatives (available models + pad/truncate). not silently downsample.

product_beth: on response format: customers prefer a simple list of embeddings (array of floats) per input for readability. but transmitting floats is heavy. we should support optional binary encoding (base64 of float32) behind a header like `Accept: application/x-emb-f32` for enterprise customers.

jamal: binary option is fine. but note: many clients use JS/TS — prefer base64 payload with typed arrays. provide examples in SDKs.

matt: rough API sketch:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "rw-embed-4096",
  "inputs": ["text1", "text2", ...],
  "shape_mode": "strict|pad|truncate",
  "encoding": "json|base64"
}

Response (json):
{
  "data": [ {"embedding": [...], "dim": 4096}, ... ],
  "model": "rw-embed-4096"
}
```

sasha: +1, but emphasize `dim` on each item only for debugging — our guarantee is that all items equal the requested dimension when shape_mode=strict or pad. we should reject requests where items*dim exceed the server ceiling with 413 and a human-friendly message and suggested split size.

product_beth: rollout plan: default behavior for existing clients (no shape_mode) => keep legacy dim (1024) for N weeks, then deprecate with clear warnings in headers + release notes. new clients must choose model/dim explicitly.

jamal: on model selection: maintain a mapping table: requested_dim -> preferred_model. e.g., 512 -> rw-embed-512, 1024 -> rw-embed-1024, 2048 -> rw-embed-2048, 4096 -> rw-embed-4096. if requested dim not supported, return 422 with suggestions. allow `model` override to pick cross-dim model (but validate compatibility).

ana (ana): cost considerations: 4096 dim = ~4x token compute vs 1024. we should gate large-dim usage via quotas and surface billing estimates in the response header `X-Emb-Cost-Estimate` for large batch requests.

matt: benchmarks: need perf matrix (latency/throughput) for each model+dim at batch sizes 1,8,32,64. i'll add to the perf doc. also we should add automatic quantization suggestion in Optimize: recommend q4_0 for 4096 workloads to customers who opt-in.

sasha: tests: integration tests should cover strict/pad/truncate modes, binary encoding, 413 split hint, and model fallback 422 message. add an end-to-end test that uploads vectors into FAISS to ensure downstream shape expectations.

product_beth: UX: SDKs should expose `shape_mode` with clear defaults and warnings. docs: migration guide for 1024->2048->4096 (including storage, index, and cost guidance).

matt: edge case: streaming / incremental embeddings where a single logical document yields multiple chunks. ensure the `dim` is stable across chunks or else reject.

jamal: ops: will add rate limiter config per-dim bucket and an alert if memory usage > 70% on embed nodes. also add a canary to ensure pad mode doesn't blow up disks.

ana (ana): action items:
- ana: write the spec PR w/ proposed API + error codes + rollout plan. (owner: ana)
- matt: perf matrix + server-side validators + max_items enforcement. (owner: matt)
- sasha: integration tests + SDK examples for base64 binary encoding. (owner: sasha)
- jamal: quota/rate-limit config + ops alerts. (owner: jamal)
- product_beth: docs + migration guide + customer comms. (owner: product_beth)

product_beth: timeline: aim to merge spec by EOD Thu, implement core validators next sprint, then beta to a handful of customers for 2 weeks.

ana (ana): sounds good. thanks everyone. tagging for visibility @matt @sasha @jamal :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-notify: bench-run-embeddings-matrix started by matt at 1809954300.
